timing.//clock: The part is specified at 2.2-2.4 GHz and this file advertises 2200 MHz to the guest through KFD. The modelled rate is kept separate on purpose: the advertised rate is what the guest divides by, the modelled rate is what produces the cycles, and silently fusing them turns a clock edit into a model change.

machine.//compute_units: The count the device ADVERTISES (simd_count 1024 / simd_per_cu 4), not the 288 this file's topology instantiates. A guest sizes its grid against the advertised number, so that is the one a throughput bound divides by.
machine.//simd_lanes: A CDNA SIMD is 16 lanes wide, so a wave64 instruction is four passes.
machine.//issue_cycles: Per-pass issue occupancy, multiplied by passes. vector_alu 1 therefore gives the familiar four cycles per wave64 VALU instruction per SIMD. unknown.issue_cycles is deliberately absent: leaving it unnamed makes the host resolve it to the largest cost here, which is the point of InstClass::Unknown. Naming it would be a way to make an unclassified opcode cheap.
machine.//ports: Units per compute unit: four SIMDs, one of everything else. The 'none' entry is the front-end issue slot every instruction occupies whatever unit it goes to, so a wait or an s_nop is not free.
machine.//global: A measured floor from the reference kernel corpus rather than the 8192-bit x 1900 MHz peak this file describes. A peak rate silently rewrites every bandwidth-heavy kernel, and a config carrying one is indistinguishable from a config that was correlated.
machine.//lds: 128 bytes per clock per compute unit.
machine.//dispatch_latency_cycles: The shortest a dispatch can take: roughly one trip through the pipeline for one wavefront, which is dominated by a memory round trip. This model has no latency model at all, so the floor is the only place that cost appears; left at zero, a kernel short enough to fit in one round trip would be reported as free.
